questions.q: Sidelights beside a door need which glass?
questions.n: They sit in a hazardous impact zone.

questions.q: Hollow molded-skin doors are best kept for:
questions.n: They're light and cheap but not weather- or force-resistant.

questions.q: Curtain wall frames are usually extruded:
questions.n: Aluminum is light, corrosion-resistant and easy to extrude.

questions.q: The glazed or louvered panel above a door, below the head or lintel, is the:
questions.n: A transom admits light and air above the door.

questions.q: Why must emergency exit doors swing outward?
o: So a crowd pushing toward the exit doesn't block the door shut
questions.n: Doors that open in the direction of travel can't be jammed closed by people pressing against them.

questions.q: The continuous step cut into a door frame that the leaf closes against, blocking light and sound, is the:
questions.n: The rabbet is the frame's stop recess; an astragal covers the meeting stiles of a pair of doors.

questions.q: Reflective glass gets its mirror effect from a thin ______ coating.
questions.n: Sputtered metal oxide layers reflect light and heat.

questions.q: Which is NOT a standard stainless steel finish name?
questions.n: Stainless finishes are named hairline, satin, brushed and mirror.

questions.q: The budget option for a display case is:
questions.n: Plain annealed glass is the cheapest.

questions.q: Panels that slide on parallel tracks and stack behind one another to leave a wide opening are:
questions.n: Each leaf runs on its own track and stacks to one side.

questions.q: The push bar across an emergency exit door is a ______ device.
questions.n: Panic bars release the latch with body pressure.

questions.q: For a bank's teller line or vault-front glazing, specify:
questions.n: The interlayer holds the glass together even after it breaks.

questions.q: A flush door has which of these visible parts?
questions.n: A flush door is a plain slab; rails, stiles and muntins belong to panel doors.

questions.q: Air leaks around operable windows and doors are sealed with:
questions.n: Caulk seals fixed joints; weatherstripping seals moving ones.

questions.q: French windows are typically all of these EXCEPT:
questions.n: Large divided glazed doors leak heat and air; energy efficiency is not their trait.

questions.q: Glass with a photocatalytic, water-loving coating that breaks down dirt and sheets it off with rain is:
questions.n: Titanium-dioxide coatings oxidize grime in sunlight.

questions.q: Which is NOT required on a one-hour fire door?
questions.n: Panic hardware depends on the occupancy, not the fire rating.

questions.q: A hinge that mortises fully into both jamb and door edge and disappears when closed is:
questions.n: Invisible hinges hide inside both members.

questions.q: Which glass cuts infrared and UV but lets most visible light through?
questions.n: Low-emissivity coatings are spectrally selective.

questions.q: Overhead glazing such as skylights and glass domes should be:
questions.n: If overhead glass breaks, laminated glass stays in place instead of falling.

questions.q: A projecting window of four or more panels set in a gentle curve is a:
questions.n: Bow windows curve; bay windows are angled, usually with three panels.

questions.q: For heavy, frequently used doors, specify butt hinges that are:
questions.n: Bearings carry the load and reduce wear.

questions.q: Standard cup-hole diameter for concealed cabinet hinges:
questions.n: Euro hinges use a 35 mm cup.

questions.q: A storefront wants no visible hardware, with glass captured along its whole top and bottom edge in concealed steel. Which component?
questions.n: U-channels grip the full edge out of sight.

questions.q: Elevator hoistway and car enclosures, and glass floors you walk on, call for:
questions.n: These need post-breakage containment, which laminated glass gives.

questions.q: The round ornamental plate behind a doorknob is the:
questions.n: Roses ring the spindle; escutcheons surround keyholes.

questions.q: The vertical side members of a door or window frame, which carry the hinges or tracks, are the:
questions.n: Jambs are the frame's sides; the head is the top.

questions.q: On the top floors of a tower, wind pressure is highest. The curtain-wall glass up there is usually:
questions.n: Higher wind loads call for thicker panes to limit deflection.

questions.q: Flexural strength of glass is its resistance to:
questions.n: Wind load bends the pane.

questions.q: "Rough hardware" refers to hardware that is:
questions.n: Finish hardware is the visible part.

questions.q: The durable plate at the bottom of a heavily used door is the:
questions.n: It protects the leaf from scuffs.

questions.q: Large frameless glass walls stiffened by perpendicular glass blades are:
questions.n: Glass fins give rigid, nearly invisible lateral support.

questions.q: Inset, full overlay and half overlay are options of which hinge?
questions.n: Cabinet hinges come in these crank variations.

questions.q: A jewelry display case needs the clearest possible glass with no green tint. Choose:
questions.n: Low-iron glass removes the green cast.

questions.q: Light-directing glass block works best placed:
questions.n: Prisms redirect daylight upward and deeper into the room.

questions.q: Graphicoat is a brand of:
questions.n: Color is fired or coated on the back face.

questions.q: Ordinary float glass looks slightly ______ at its edge because of iron in the batch.
questions.n: Iron oxide gives the green tint; low-iron glass removes it.

questions.q: The beam over an opening that carries the wall above is the:
questions.n: A lintel spans the opening and carries the load above.

questions.q: Privacy locksets suit all of these EXCEPT:
questions.n: Passage sets have no lock.

questions.q: Heat-treated glass about twice as strong as float that still breaks into large shards is:
questions.n: Heat-strengthened glass is not a safety glass; it breaks like annealed glass.
